patches.find: ⚠ This shows relative elevation, not a computed sightline. A genuine viewshed analysis needs full terrain elevation data (a digital elevation raster) plus real obstruction modeling for hills, woods, buildings, and smoke -- this deployment doesn't have access to that. Earlier drafts of this tool tried a distance-to-horizon formula based on elevation alone, but that produced 30+ mile "visibility" circles that are physically correct as pure earth-curvature math yet meaningless at this battlefield's actual ~5-mile scale, where nearby terrain -- not the curve of the earth -- is what actually blocked a soldier's view. So instead: below is each vantage point's real elevation, ranked against the other 29 mapped locations, so you can see genuine high-ground advantage without a fabricated distance claim.
patches.repl: ⚠ Elevation only. This page ranks the height of 30 places on the field. It is not a line-of-sight map: trees, buildings, fences and gun smoke often decided what a soldier could see.

patches.find: This needs a phone: its camera, GPS, and compass, all live, granted directly in your browser. Nothing is uploaded -- your camera feed and location never leave your device. This is a real, working implementation, but its on-the-ground accuracy can only be confirmed by testing it while actually standing at Gettysburg, which we haven't been able to do from here.
patches.repl: Beta. Battlefield AR needs a phone with a camera, GPS and compass, and works best outdoors on the field. Your camera view and location stay on your device; nothing is uploaded. Compass accuracy varies by phone, so treat the markers as a guide to direction, not a survey. This page is not listed in the site menu while it is being tested.
